Explosives: TNT and dynamite

TNT and dynamite break blocks in a wide circle. Blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected. Creative players can use them freely. In Survival you craft both from sand, Charcoal, boards and Paper screens.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents

  2. How far a blast reaches
  3. Damage and knockback
  4. Throw dynamite
  5. Crafting TNT and dynamite in Survival

Place and light TNT

  1. Select TNT in your hotbar.
  2. Right click a surface to place a whole block. Hold Shift and right click to place one half-metre charge.
  3. Aim at the TNT, within 6 m, and press G.
  4. Step back. The fuse lasts 2.6 seconds.
Key or actionWhat it does
Right clickPlace a whole TNT block.
Shift + right clickPlace one half-metre charge.
GLight the aimed TNT and every TNT piece touching it, even diagonally.
Left clickMine TNT back without lighting it.

Lit TNT pops loose and can fall, roll or float before it blows. Touching pieces go off together as one blast. One press lights at most 64 whole blocks (512 pieces). TNT: place and ignite (G)

Good to know. On a multiplayer server, G asks the server to light the TNT. The status line says "Requesting TNT ignition | move away"; wait for the reply before your next action. The server checks that you can reach the TNT, and that no piece of the group is on land you may not build on or holds up furniture. It then says, for example, "8-charge TNT cluster ignited by server | move away". A refusal starts with "TNT ignition refused:" and gives the reason. If the server restarts while a fuse burns, that TNT is lost.

How far a blast reaches

  • One half-metre charge or one dynamite stick: about 1.5 m.
  • One whole TNT block: about 4.25 m.
  • A touching group of TNT: up to about 10.5 m, which needs about 62 touching TNT blocks.

A whole TNT block cannot break obsidian. Solid stone only gives way close to the charge. Blocks between the charge and a target absorb part of the blast, and water absorbs a lot of it. Water is never destroyed, and chests survive every blast. Other TNT inside the blast is lit on a short fuse of under a second and thrown outward. Explosions: reach, damage and terrain

Good to know. In a single-player world a blast breaks your own builds too. On a multiplayer server it leaves doors, chests and the blocks that hold up furniture alone, breaks nothing on land the person who lit it may not build on, and does not hurt players or animals standing there.
Careful. Explosions cannot be undone. Blasted blocks are gone. The status line counts cleared half-metre voxels.

Damage and knockback

In Survival, players near a blast lose health and are knocked back. Creative players take no damage and are not pushed. Creatures are hurt in both modes. In Survival, an animal killed by a blast drops its items on the ground; in Creative it is removed.

Damage reaches about one and a half times as far as the blast breaks blocks: about 2.3 m for a half-metre charge or dynamite stick, about 6.6 m for one TNT block and about 16 m for the largest group. It is strongest close to the charge, and walls between you and the charge reduce it.

Tip. Stand well back before you light a group. Damage reaches about 16 m from the largest group.

Throw dynamite

  1. Select Dynamite in your hotbar.
  2. Hold right click to wind up. A longer wind-up throws farther; full power takes 0.7 seconds.
  3. Release to throw. The fuse starts on release.
  4. Take cover. The stick goes off 2.3 seconds after you throw it, wherever it is then.
Key or actionWhat it does
Right click (hold, then release)Wind up and throw a dynamite stick.
  • The stick sticks to the first surface it hits, including walls, ceilings and furniture. If that surface is dug or blown away, the stick falls again.
  • A very short wind-up does not throw. The status line says "Too hasty — wind up before releasing".
  • You cannot place blocks while you hold dynamite.
  • Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.
  • Creative throws are unlimited. Survival uses one stick per throw. A throw that cannot fly keeps the stick.
  • On a multiplayer server, releasing asks the server to throw. The status line says "Requesting dynamite throw", then "Dynamite thrown by server". Wait for the reply before you throw again. A refused throw keeps the stick, for example "Wait for the server to finish the current action | dynamite kept". In Survival the server spends one stick when it accepts the throw; Creative throws stay free.

Crafting TNT and dynamite in Survival

Tools & arms 2 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
TNT8× TNT
  • 32× Sand
  • 8× Charcoal
  • 8× Boards of any species (mixable)

Makes one full TNT block (8 pieces) from 4 blocks of Sand, one block of Charcoal and one block of boards.

Two dynamite sticks2× Dynamite
  • 4× TNT
  • 2× Paper screen

Needs half a block of TNT (4 pieces).

One TNT recipe makes 8 pieces, one whole block. Two dynamite sticks need 4 TNT pieces and 2 Paper screens. Neither recipe needs Glow crystal. Glow-crystal recipes in survival

What a quit or reload does

  • Lit TNT and burning dynamite are not saved. Quitting during a fuse loses that TNT.
  • On a multiplayer server, lit TNT and burning dynamite are lost if the server restarts. Blasted ground, injuries and loot are kept.
  • Explosions are not recorded in build history.
